ops.title: Client's six seams are deleted and the coverage they enabled is paid for; the trust E2E follows launchd out of the suite
ops.body:
Decided by yasyf, 2026-08-03, closing the de-fake sweep. Two answers.

## 1. Delete the six Client seams, and accept the coverage loss

Client.{probe, observe, identities, readOwner, kill, serving} go, along with deploy.{verify, run,
inventory}, assemblePins probe/health params, and internal/proc/inventory.gos list/executable/
probe params. Production calls the real function; tests stand up real instances.

**This is not free and was not chosen as if it were.** 62 test assignment sites exist
(ensure_test.go 44, control_test.go 10, settle_test.go 2, internal/proc/observe_test.go 6). The
de-fake sweep deliberately KEPT these and left its reasoning at ensure_test.go:1057 — a real store
records only the process that opens it, so a stale, departed, or cross-boot owner record has no
other way into a test. Roughly 8 test functions assert states a live machine cannot be asked to
produce (cross-boot record, stale-start record, unnameable husk, wedged incumbent kill ladder), and
scripts/e2e-launchd.sh cannot absorb them either — real launchd cannot furnish a cross-boot record.
That coverage dies rather than moves.

Weighed against: directive 44bcb88, and the fact that this same family of seams is what let PID
4242 — a process that never existed — look alive and carry two ensure tests to a green pass for as
long as it did. The principle wins.

**Do NOT delete beforeWrite (internal/wire/session.go:89,709) or release (server.go:341).** My
"zero non-test assignments" scan produced two false positives. sendAdmittedResponse (session.go:698)
supplies a real beforeWrite closure that sets terminalSent under the mutex before the frame reaches
the wire — an ordering invariant with zero test references — and server.go:302 passes release into
serveSession, wrapped in sync.OnceFunc against sessionWG.Done(). The scan collided with adopt.go:89s
unrelated `release: releaseGate` Gate field. launchd/apply.go:111 wait also stays: production
supplies waitRetry at three sites (apply.go:68,88,105), so it is not test-only, and it is a clock
boundary STYLEGUIDE § Testing sanctions.

The test that decides membership is unchanged: does production ever supply a value.

## 2. The signed-peer trust E2E leaves the suite, exactly as launchd did

verify_signed_test.go and scripts/trust-fixtures.sh become scripts/e2e-trust.sh, run by whoever
holds a Developer ID. DAEMONKIT_TRUST_E2E is deleted — the gate disappears because the test leaves,
not because it was made conditional. Closes the standing task "G4: give the signed-peer E2E a CI
home": it has no home in CI, by measurement.

**Correcting my own premise in 39c8faf**, which said "/usr/bin/codesign is present on every machine
that can build this darwin-only module" and concluded the trust E2E could therefore always run.
codesigns presence is not an identitys. Measured: `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` →
0 valid identities; docs/BUILD-ORDER.md:43 records the same independently; deploy_test.go:119 notes
no CI runner can mint one. Ad-hoc signing yields `TeamIdentifier=not set`, flags 0x2(adhoc), while
verifyToken (internal/trust/verify.go:40) requires a matching teamID and checkValidationCategory
requires category 6 (Developer ID). The deploy lanes ad-hoc signing works only because it relaxes
its DR to an identifier clause alone and asserts neither. Deleting the gate would have turned
internal/trust permanently red, and its 11 reject cases would have passed for the wrong reason —
category, not the property under test.

The kernel-path trust coverage is unaffected: fakeKernel feeds real CMS chains and real
CodeDirectories through the real verifyToken, which is a csops syscall-boundary mock, not a lie.
